school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Columbia's Morningside Heights and Manhattanville campuses, from the historic 'Frat Row' to the modern developments of 125th Street.

cards.title: The Main Commercial Strip
cards.subtitle: Broadway Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this stretch to find student staples like Tom's Restaurant and Book Culture. It serves as the primary retail and dining artery for the Morningside Heights community.
cards.short_summary: The primary commercial corridor for Columbia students, featuring historic diners, bookstores, and essential retail.
cards.evidence_claim: Broadway and Amsterdam Avenue are the main commercial streets in the area, offering a variety of food markets, restaurants, shops and bookstores.
cards.access_notes: Public city street with 24/7 sidewalk access; business hours vary by establishment.

cards.title: The Cathedral District
cards.subtitle: Amsterdam Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Hungarian Pastry Shop for a study session across from the Cathedral of St. John the Divine. This area offers a quieter, more scenic alternative to Broadway.
cards.short_summary: A scenic stretch of Amsterdam Avenue home to the world's largest cathedral and popular student study cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cathedral of Saint John the Divine is located a few blocks away from campus between 113th and 110th Street, across from the popular Hungarian Pastry Shop.
cards.source_title: A guide to Morningside Heights as a Columbia student
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; the Cathedral grounds are generally open to the public during daylight hours.

cards.title: Historic Frat Row
cards.subtitle: West 114th Street
cards.notes: Pass by the historic brownstones housing Columbia's Greek life. This residential block is a hub for student social activity and sits directly south of Butler Library.
cards.short_summary: Known as 'Frat Row,' this block features many of the university's fraternity and sorority brownstones.
cards.evidence_claim: Frat Row is the stretch of 114th St between Broadway and Amsterdam where a lot of fraternities and sororities are located.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; brownstone interiors are restricted to residents and invited guests.

cards.title: The Manhattanville Gateway
cards.subtitle: 125th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the new Manhattanville campus expansion, featuring the Jerome L. Greene Science Center and the Forum. It connects the university to the heart of West Harlem.
cards.short_summary: The northern anchor of Columbia's expansion, featuring modern architecture and public community spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Manhattanville campus spans 17 acres from 125th Street to 134th Street between Broadway and 12th Avenue.
cards.source_title: Manhattanville campus construction continues into its 17th year
cards.access_notes: Public street; university buildings like The Forum have public-access ground floors.

cards.title: The Eastern Overlook
cards.subtitle: Morningside Drive Corridor
cards.notes: Walk along the stone wall for panoramic views of Morningside Park and Harlem. This quiet street borders the eastern edge of the Morningside Heights campus.
cards.short_summary: A scenic residential street offering elevated views of the park and the city skyline to the east.
cards.evidence_claim: Morningside Drive is the eastern boundary of Morningside Heights, overlooking Morningside Park built on a steep incline.
cards.access_notes: Public street and sidewalk; best visited during daylight for park views.

cards.title: The Residential Hub
cards.subtitle: West 113th Street
cards.notes: Find several large residence halls like 600 W 113th (Nussbaum) and McBain Hall. This block is densely populated by sophomores and juniors.
cards.short_summary: A key residential block for upperclassmen, housing several large university-owned dormitories.
cards.evidence_claim: 600 West 113th Street (Nussbaum) is a residence hall housing a mix of sophomores, juniors, and seniors.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; dorm access requires CUID swipe.

cards.title: The Western Parkside
cards.subtitle: Riverside Drive Corridor
cards.notes: Head west to this scenic drive to access Riverside Park's running paths and sunset views. It marks the western boundary of the university's neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A grand residential avenue bordering Riverside Park, popular for recreation and quiet walks.
cards.evidence_claim: Morningside Heights is bounded by Riverside Drive to the west, providing access to Riverside Park.
cards.access_notes: Public street and park access; park is open daily from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM.

cards.title: The Manhattanville Connector
cards.subtitle: LaSalle Street
cards.notes: Walk this street to see the transition between Morningside Heights and the Manhattanville campus. It houses several graduate student residences.
cards.short_summary: A short street in the northern part of the neighborhood housing several Columbia Residential buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Columbia Residential buildings like 100 LaSalle and 124 LaSalle are located in the Morningside Heights and Manhattanville area.

cards.title: The Quiet Residential Block
cards.subtitle: West 115th Street
cards.notes: Stroll past brownstones and dorms like 627 W 115th. This block offers a more residential feel just steps away from the main campus gates.
cards.short_summary: A primarily residential street housing several university-owned apartment buildings and dorms.
cards.evidence_claim: 627 W. 115th Street is a residence hall typically housing seniors and juniors.

cards.title: The Institutional Corridor
cards.subtitle: Amsterdam Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Observe the Law School and School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) buildings. The Law Bridge spans this avenue, connecting the main campus to East Campus.
cards.short_summary: A stretch of Amsterdam Avenue dominated by university academic buildings and the Law Bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: Amsterdam Avenue is mostly lined by institutional buildings owned by Columbia, as well as St. Luke's Hospital.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; the Law Bridge is accessible to CUID holders.
